summary_en: Konoike Transport will acquire all shares of NS Holdings to make it a wholly owned subsidiary, thereby making Nishin Kiko (machinery maintenance and civil engineering company) a grandchild subsidiary. The acquisition aims to strengthen the maintenance and engineering business and realize synergies by combining Nishin Kiko's cleaning technology with Konoike's construction capabilities.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Shares in NS Holdings Co., Ltd. (Making it a Wholly Owned Subsidiary) and Making Nishin Kiko Co., Ltd. a Grandchild Company
translation_en_brief:
Konoike Transport announced on November 18, 2026, that its Board of Directors resolved to acquire all shares of NS Holdings Co., Ltd., making it a wholly owned subsidiary. Through this transaction, Nishin Kiko Co., Ltd.—a company engaged in machinery maintenance and civil engineering—will become Konoike's grandchild company. The acquisition is conditional upon obtaining necessary regulatory approvals and fulfillment of other conditions stipulated in the transaction agreement.

The acquisition aligns with Konoike's mid-to-long-term growth strategy, positioning engineering services as a priority area, particularly to strengthen the maintenance and preservation business domain. Nishin Kiko is a pioneer in waterjet cleaning technology and offers comprehensive services including equipment installation, disassembly, and related services. The company has built a strong customer base centered on major enterprises and substantial track record in infrastructure projects, making it highly compatible with Konoike's engineering business.

Konoike plans to leverage Nishin Kiko's specialized cleaning technology and on-site capabilities alongside its own construction, engineering, and project management functions. By integrating Nishin Kiko's expertise with Konoike's scaffolding, equipment maintenance, and installation services, the company expects to achieve single-window customer service, reduced coordination burden, improved construction quality, and shortened equipment downtime. The acquisition also aims to expand service offerings, enable larger projects, and develop new construction methods by combining both companies' technical expertise, customer bases, and human resources.
